blocks.text: When a policy violation is detected in your cloud resources, AI Security generates issues and notifies recipients to take action. These generated issues are displayed on the Issues page. Issues that are initially generated are in Open status. When these issues are evaluated and addressed, the status transitions to Resolved, Closed, or Snoozed.
AI Security issues can have the following status:

table: Issue Status
Description
Example Scenarios
Notes
Open
The new issues generated for a policy violation or resolved issues for which policy violation is detected again.
A policy violation is detected. The policy violation is detected again within 180 days of resolving the issue.

An open issue moves to the resolved, closed, or snoozed state based on the latest policy findings, manual actions (resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset), or issue filter (ignore issue filter). When a data store is removed from the scan settings, the issues remain open based on the posture assessment of the data store. An automatically resolved issue is reopened if the violation is detected within 180 days of resolving the issue. The Issue Status Reason in an individual issue's page describes the reason why the issue is reopened. AI Security generates a new issue if the policy violation is detected again after 180 days.
Closed
The issues that are no longer valid.

The cloud account is offboarded. The cloud account is deleted from the CSP. The policy is edited, disabled, or deleted. The data store is deleted. The data store that was removed earlier is not added back to the scan settings.

A closed issue is the final state of an issue (i.e., it does not move to any other state). The issue graph for a closed issue is frozen and the nodes are unclickable. The Sensitive Data tab in an individual issue's page is hidden. The closed issue is deleted from the AI Security Admin Portal after 180 days.
Resolved
The policy violation detected in the data store is fixed.
The issue is manually resolved in the AI Security Admin Portal. The policy violation is manually remediated. The policy violation is resolved in the CSP.

An automatically resolved issue moves to the open state if the issue is detected within 180 days of resolving the issue. AI Security generates a new issue if the policy violation is detected again after 180 days. A manually resolved issue remains in the resolved state until you reset it. When you reset the issue, the issue status is updated based on the latest policy findings. A resolved issue moves to the closed state if the data store, policy, or cloud account is deleted. The issue graph for a resolved issue is frozen, and the nodes are unclickable. The Sensitive Data tab in an individual issue's page is hidden.
Snoozed
Issues of low priority that are paused for a specific duration.
The issue is manually snoozed to pause notification for a specified duration.

A snoozed issue remains snoozed even if the policy violation is resolved in the CSP. If you unsnooze an issue or if the snooze period expires, the issue status changes to open or resolved based on the latest policy findings. If the data store or policy is deleted when the issue is snoozed, the issue moves to the closed state irrespective of the snooze period. If the policy violation is resolved in the CSP, the issue graph freezes, and the nodes become unclickable.
